methodology: To decompose the original research topic and the generated technical specification into atomic units, I systematically analyzed both texts to identify distinct requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was defined as an independent and self-contained statement that is technically specific and unambiguous. I focused on ensuring that each unit could be implemented as a single requirement, which allowed for clear comparisons between the two sets of information. The decomposition process involved reading through both documents, highlighting key actions and conditions, and then rephrasing them into concise atomic statements.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Lemmings can be in one of two states: walking left (walk_left = 1) or walking right (walk_right = 1).
Lemmings switch directions when bumped: bump_left causes walking right, and bump_right causes walking left.
If bumped on both sides simultaneously, Lemmings still switch directions.
When ground = 0, Lemmings fall and say 'aaah!'.
When ground = 1, Lemmings resume walking in the same direction as before the fall.
Being bumped while falling does not affect walking direction.
Being bumped when ground disappears or reappears while falling does not affect walking direction.
Lemmings can dig when dig = 1, but only if ground = 1 and not falling.
Lemmings continue digging until they reach ground = 0.
If a Lemming falls for more than 20 clock cycles and hits the ground, it splatters and ceases all actions.
Lemmings do not splatter in mid-air.
Implement a Moore state machine to model this behavior.
The areset signal triggers an asynchronous reset to walk left.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs for clk, areset, bump_left, bump_right, ground, and dig.
Outputs include walk_left, walk_right, aaah, and digging.
Direction Control Logic determines walking direction based on bump inputs.
Falling Logic manages the falling state based on the ground input.
Digging Logic allows for digging when conditions are met.
Splatter Logic ensures Lemming ceases all actions after falling for too long.
The logic prioritizes falling over digging, which takes precedence over direction changes.
The Lemming can be in one of two states: walking left (walk_left = 1) or walking right (walk_right = 1).
If bump_left = 1, then walk_right = 1 and walk_left = 0; if bump_right = 1, then walk_left = 1 and walk_right = 0.
If both bumps are active, the Lemming switches directions.
The falling state is activated when ground = 0, setting aaah = 1.
When ground = 1, the Lemming resumes walking in the last direction.
The digging state is activated when dig = 1, but only if ground = 1 and not falling.
The Lemming will dig until it encounters ground = 0, at which point it will fall.
The splatter condition is checked after 20 cycles of falling; if exceeded, all outputs are set to 0.
The design ensures that fall has the highest precedence, followed by dig, and then direction changes.
